CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 25
The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. to guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of assurance of safety from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. to establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. to provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus that administer governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER VIII
PARTICIPATION
Article 33
(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.
(2) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or social community organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, business entities and other related stakeholders.
(3) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women; and

(1) The Regional Government conducts coordination in handling protection services for women victims of violence, exploitation, and discrimination at the sub-district level by establishing a women and children protection forum.
(2) The membership of the women and children protection forum as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements from the Sub-district, Sector Police, Military District Command, Community Health Center, Office of Religious Affairs and other elements.

Integrated Service is the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizer to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women and children protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

NUMBER 01 YEAR 2025
CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Second Part
UPTD PPA
Article 28
(1) The Regional Government, in an effort to provide and administer handling services for the protection of women victims of violence, exploitation, and violent acts, establishes the UPTD PPA.
(2) The UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) is under and accountable to the head of the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
(3) Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties and functions, as well as the management of the UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

(3) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women and children protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

Article 33
(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(3) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;

Article 29

I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

CHAPTER I

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

Integrated Service is the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women and children protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Article 26
Regional Government is responsible for:
a. implementing policies, programs, activities for the administration of protection and empowerment of women in order to realize the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure for the administration of protection and empowerment of women; and
c. applying service standards for the administration of protection and empowerment of women in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

NUMBER 01 YEAR 2025
CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 25
The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. to guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of assurance of safety from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. to establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. to provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus that administer governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER VIII
PARTICIPATION
Article 33
(1) Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in the Region.

(3) Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of: a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women; and
c. conducting skills training.

I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 25
The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:

Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Article 20
The Implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of employment as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter c number 5 is carried out by Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of labor and related agencies in the form of:
a. provision of skills and job training;
b. women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment; and
c. employers who employ female workers, provide access and skills training.

Article 18
The implementation of women's empowerment in the economic field as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter c number 3 shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of micro, small and medium enterprises and related agencies in the form of:
a. facilitation of the establishment and strengthening of productive economic business groups; and
b. facilitation of marketing network development.

Article 22
What is meant by related agencies are agencies that have a role in the implementation of women's empowerment in the social field, which may include women and children protection institutions, legal aid organizations and assistance for victims of violence, safe houses (shelters) that handle gender-based violence victims, psychology practitioners and counselors, universities/educational institutions, community organizations, Family Welfare Empowerment, gender study centers at universities, family counseling consultation institutions, religious organizations that have women's empowerment programs, social rehabilitation centers.

In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 25
The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. to guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of assurance of safety from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. to establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. to provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus that administer governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

Article 29
(1) The Regional Government conducts coordination in handling protection services for women victims of violence, exploitation, and discrimination at the sub-district level by establishing a women and children protection forum.
(2) The membership of the women and children protection forum as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of elements from the Sub-district, Sector Police, Military District Command, Community Health Center, Office of Religious Affairs and other elements.

Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

CONCERNING
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN
I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Article 25
The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. to guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of assurance of safety from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. to establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and

Article 25
The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. to guarantee the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of assurance of safety from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. to establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. to provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus that administer governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

Integrated Service is the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizer to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health problems they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/area where violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an action with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnicity, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that organizes government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women and children protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women and children protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional People's Representative Council hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional People's Representative Council of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Woman is a person of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who has been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can regulate themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any action that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and obstructing the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or limits the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control over the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, limiting or prohibiting the victim from having or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons intended for sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and their children, or mother and their children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights is a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

I. GENERAL
Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to education services, health, employment, as well as participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is formulated as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a system that is fair, inclusive, and in favor of vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, fulfill the special needs of women, as well as improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.
It is expected that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts as well as encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.
